matches.snippet: g Amendments 2−16−2005: 233 (d)  (i) Each day of a continuing violation of the provisions described in Subsection 234 73−2−25(2)(a) or an initial or final order issued under Section 73−2−25 is a separate violation. (ii) A penalty may not be imposed for a violation of the provisions listed in Subsection 73−2−25(2)(a) or an initial or a final order issued under Section 73−2−25 for a violation occurring more than 12 months before the day on which a notice of violation is issued. Senator Peterson’s motion to amend passed on a voice vote. Senators Hillyard and Thomas commented and the bill passed on the following roll call: Y eas, 25; Nays, 0; Absent, 4. (Ord. 04-224, 8-16-2004)  3-5-6: FAILURE TO CONTROL NOXIOUS WEEDS; LIABILITY OF  PROPERTY OWNER:      A. Authority Of County: If the owner or person in possession of the property fails to take action to  control or prevent the spread of noxious weeds within five (5) working days after the property is  declared a public nuisance, the weed control supervisor or authorized agent may, after  reasonable notification, enter the property, without the consent of the owner or the person in  possession, and perform any work necessary, consistent with sound weed prevention and  control practices, to control the weeds.    B. Responsibility For Expenses; Lien: Any expense incurred by the county in controlling the noxious  weeds is paid by the property owner of record
